Three bytes of code in zero page, `inc $E0 / rts`, put there by the loader's last stage ($B005 copies them from $B0EF): the routine irq_trampoline calls while speech plays, so that the tick still counts.

Speech sample buffer, built at run time: the frame decoders ($0A68, $0AE5, $0B73, $0BE3) write one frame's volume levels here ($0800-$087F, 32 or 128 entries), and $0BFD writes an averaged copy at $0820. The NMI handlers read it through the self-modified operand of `lda $0860` at $0884/$08A5. In play it holds the last frame of the last phrase; at the game's start it held a copy of $0880-$08FF left by the unpacker.

Speech driver entry, the only address the game calls ($BEF7, $BF08): jumps to speech_command at $0C2F. A = phrase number, or $FF (ask whether a phrase is playing), $FE (stop), $FD (set the sample base address from X/Y).

NMI handler, phase 1 of a sample period: takes the next level from the speech buffer (operand $0885 is the index, stepped up by one each NMI), halves it and writes it to the SID volume register $D418, which with no voice sounding makes the level audible as a sample. Acknowledges CIA 2 ($DD0D). Counts $AD down; when it reaches 0 it switches the NMI vector to nmi_speech_down ($08A4) and hands the index on to it.
Operand low byte of `lda $0860` in nmi_speech_up: the speech buffer index, stepped up each NMI ($0892) and set from $0CF2 at each period ($08FB).

NMI handler, phase 2: plays the buffer backwards from where phase 1 stopped (operand $08A6 stepped down), counting $AE. With $AF zero the period ends (speech_next_period at $08F2); otherwise it switches to nmi_speech_hold ($08C3).
Operand low byte of `lda $0860` in nmi_speech_down: the index stepped down, taken over from nmi_speech_up ($089F).
NMI handler, phase 3: writes a fixed level 7 ($0E halved) to $D418, a silent gap, for $AF timer periods, switching to nmi_speech_wait ($08D9) after the first.
NMI handler for the rest of the silent gap: acknowledges the timer and counts $AF down without touching the volume; at 0 goes on to speech_next_period ($08F1).
NMI handler installed when a phrase ends: stops CIA 2 timer A ($DD0F = $90), leaves the volume at 7 and returns. No further NMIs follow until the next phrase starts the timer.

Start of the next pitch period, entered from the NMI handlers: reloads the handler chain from the driver's variables ($0CF1 next handler, $0CF2 buffer start index, $0CF3 phase lengths into $AD/$AE, $0CF4 gap into $AF). Counts frames in $0CF7; when a frame is used up it advances the frame counter $0CF5, fetches the next frame header (speech_frame_header at $09B6 when $0CF5 wraps) and calls the decoder whose address is patched into the `jsr` at $092E. Otherwise it steps the pitch (speech_pitch_step at $0B1D) and, when the buffer start changed, rebuilds the smoothed half of the buffer ($0BFD).
Operand low byte of the `jmp $0939` in speech_next_period: $39 for the normal tail, $51 for the window shift ($0951), $37 for repeat frames; written by the frame-header code.
Operand low byte of the `jsr $097B` in speech_next_period: selects the frame decoder ($8C, $8F, $92, $98) or the end ($7B) or the start gap ($81).

Alternative tail of speech_next_period, selected by patching the `jmp` at $0910 to $0951: moves the playback window ($0CF2) forward by $0CF9 and shortens the phase length $0CF3 by the same until it reaches 16, then resets both.
Makes nmi_speech_end ($08E1) the next handler: the phrase is finished. Selected as the decoder of speech_next_period when the phrase's last frame is reached.
Sets the next handler to nmi_speech_hold ($08C3) with a gap of $80 periods; used at the start of a phrase.
Entry stub of the decoder table patched into $092F: jumps to the 1-bit decoder at $0B73.
Entry stub: jumps to the 1-bit decoder's continuation at $0BE3.
Entry stub: 2-bit decoder ($0A68), then the common frame end at $099B.
Entry stub: 4-bit decoder ($0AE5), then falls into speech_frame_end.

After a frame is decoded: if bit 7 of the frame's flags ($09B7) is set, flips the buffer half (bit 6) and restarts the window; otherwise rebuilds the smoothed copy ($0BFD). Then steps the pitch ($0B1D).

Reads the next 4-byte frame header from ($A5): byte 0 = frame count ($0CF5, ORed with $C0) and flags, byte 1 = repeat count and encoding (bits 0-1 select the decoder: 0/1 the 1-bit decoders, 2/3 the 2-bit and 4-bit), bytes 2-3 = offset of the frame's sample data from the sample base ($0CFE/$0CFF) into $A9/$AA. A first byte with bit 7 clear (the operand at $09B7 is patched to $7B) ends the phrase. Patches the decoder `jsr` at $092E and the `jmp` at $0910, then steps $A5 by 4.

Immediate operand of `lda #$8F` in speech_frame_header: holds the current frame header's flag byte (bit 7 set while frames remain; bit 6 the buffer half), written by the decoders and the frame-repeat code.
Four phase lengths for the 2-bit and 4-bit encodings ($08, $10, $18, $20), chosen by the top two bits of the frame's first byte at $0A2E.
Frame header path for a repeated frame: takes the flags from header byte 3 and selects the window-shift tail ($0911 = $37) and the start-gap handler ($092F = $81).

2-bit decoder: each byte of sample data holds four 2-bit codes; each code picks one of four levels from the level table chosen by the byte's low two bits ($0AD9, $0ADD or $0AE1, pointer in $AB/$AC). Fills the speech buffer $0800,x up to the length patched into $0AD5.
Immediate operand of `lda #$00` in speech_dec_2bit: the current data byte, saved there ($0A75, $0A96) and read back for its next 2-bit fields.
Operand of `cpx #$00` in speech_dec_2bit: the end of the frame in the buffer, set from the window length ($0A6B, $0BE9).
Three level tables of four volume levels each (doubled, halved again on output) for the 2-bit decoder: $0C-$12 (quiet, narrow), $08-$14, $02-$1A (loud, wide).
4-bit decoder: each byte of sample data holds two 4-bit levels (masked to even values with AND #$1E); fills the buffer up to the length patched into $0B19 (32 by default).
Operand of `cpx #$20` in speech_dec_4bit: the frame's end in the buffer, set at $0AE8.

Steps the pitch once per period: while the count $0CFB runs, adds the step $0CFD to the period length $0CFC and sets the gap $0CF4 to half of it. When the count runs out, reads the next pitch command from ($A7): a new period length, a 4-bit count and a 4-bit index into tbl_speech_pitch ($0B63) for the new step.
Sixteen signed pitch steps for speech_pitch_step: -12, -10, ... -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, ... 14 (two's complement $F4-$0E).
1-bit decoder: each bit of sample data gives one of two levels, $0E or $10, so the waveform moves up or down by one step around the middle. Writes the buffer up to the length patched into $0BAB.
Operand of `cpx #$80` in speech_dec_1bit: the frame's end in the buffer, set at $0B79.
Writes four buffer entries from the low four bits of A, one per bit: $10 for a 1, $0E for a 0.
Second entry of speech_put_bits: writes the level already in A and the remaining two bits of Y; used by speech_dec_1bit for the first byte of a frame.
Continues a 1-bit frame: sets the window start and length, then rejoins the 2-bit decoder's loop at $0A75 with a flag that keeps the levels.
Builds the averaged half of the speech buffer: for each of $0CF3 entries, the mean of $0800,x and $0860,x (with a self-modified base) goes to $0820,x, which softens the step between two frames.
Operand low byte of `lda $0800,x` in speech_smooth: the start of the previous window ($0CFA).
Operand low byte of `adc $0860,x` in speech_smooth: the start of the current window ($0CF2).
Operand low byte of `sta $0820,x` in speech_smooth: where the averaged entries go, the other half of the buffer (bit 6 flipped, +$20), kept as the next window start.

The driver's command handler (called through speech_say at $0880). A = $FF: returns the playing flag (bit 7 of $DD0F's start bit, or $80 when the ROMs are banked in); $FE: stops the timer ($0C60); $FD: stores X/Y as the sample base $0CFE/$0CFF; any other value: looks up the phrase ($0CAB), sets the first gap of 10 periods, installs nmi_speech_up's chain ($0C89), points the NMI vector's high byte at page $08 and starts the timer ($0C71).
Stops CIA 2 timer A ($DD0F = $90).
Starts CIA 2 timer A in continuous mode with a latch of 100 ($64): an NMI every 101 cycles, 9,755 a second on PAL. Enables the timer NMI ($DD0D = $82) and clears any pending one.

Resets the driver for a new phrase: the `jmp` at $0910 to its normal tail, the decoder `jsr` to speech_start_gap ($0981), the frame counters to $FE, and the NMI vector's low byte to $C3 (nmi_speech_hold).

Looks up phrase A in the phrase table at the start of the sample data (base $0CFE/$0CFF, which the game sets to $E000): entry 4 × A holds two offsets, the phrase's pitch commands (into $A7/$A8) and its frame headers (into $A5/$A6), each relative to the base.

The game's entry, where the loader's unpacker jumps with $01 = $25. In the image as loaded, $3855-$3865 held `lda #$60 / sta $DD03` (CIA 2 port B direction = $60, the `rts` opcode that wait_ticks executes at $DD03), NMI RAM vector $0318 = $3854, `sei / cld`; the loop at $389C clears those 17 bytes with the sprite registers, so in play they read as zeros. Then: builds a table at $CF00 ($71C0, $3875 loop), detects PAL or NTSC ($3FB9), clears zero page $10-$DA and the SID, sets up the variables, banks the KERNAL out ($01 = $25), installs the IRQ ($82F4, via $BEC2) and the temporary IRQ $8396, enables the raster interrupt, builds the bit-reversal table at $C500, selects video bank 1 ($DD00), screen $4000 and character set $4800, copies the letters and digits of the character ROM into both character sets, draws the pocket computer and the lift, and falls into the lift loop at $39CF.
The start-up's greeting: voice line 2, a wait of 32 ticks, then voice line 3, spoken after the load and after every restart, before the title state; the agent has not been shown a room yet.

The loop that runs while the agent is in a lift or a corridor (also the title state, where the game waits in the lift): every pass waits for the frame ($83F4), updates the agent ($73E4) and fades the sound effect on voices 1 and 2 ($25/$26). Fire (debounced by $DE) with $3F = $0E opens the pocket computer ($3A80). With the agent's sprite inside the lift car (sprite 1 X $A2-$B6, high bit clear) and $3F = $0E, up on the stick moves the lift up ($8592) and down moves it down ($855C) until it stops at a floor ($1F/$20 = $0B); otherwise the agent walks ($860B).

Opens the pocket computer: clears sprites 4-6's high and multicolour bits, restores the panel ($7218), copies the puzzle display graphics into character set $5800 ($3E16), sounds a tone, draws the map and pieces ($7427, $8025), shows the hand pointer ($3E39) and the selected piece's frame ($3E9D, $3ED0). Then loops at $3AAF: waits for the frame, moves the hand with the stick ($3DC2), and on fire acts on the button under the hand. $9F says what the hand is doing: 0 = choosing a button, 1 = moving a piece in the display ($7D4C), 2 or more = dragging ($7D8C).

Main loop of the pocket computer (see $3A80). On a fresh fire press with $9F = 0, the hand's position (sprite 4: X/2 in X, Y in Y) is compared with the button grid: the right-hand block of nine at X/2 $84-$9F, Y $B1-$E8, handled from $3BDB; the three keys on the left at X/2 $13-$1B ($3C44); the four piece slots of the display ($3C74).

Fire on one of the display's six piece slots (Y = slot): with a piece there, checks that its colour matches the one the hand carries ($D02C against the colour RAM under the slot, self-modified address from $7A55/$7A5B); a mismatch prints COLORS MUST MATCH ($821E), an overlap IMAGES CAN'T OVERLAP ($8234, tested by $8037). With no piece carried it plays the error tone. An empty slot takes the carried piece: marks it used ($92,y), paints the 6×3 cells in colour RAM, plays a tone and redraws ($3F61, $3E39, $3E9D, $80C3, $3ED0).

High byte of the colour RAM address read by pc_select_slot, from tbl_slot_colour_ram_hi ($3B56).

Decodes a fire on the right-hand block of nine buttons by the hand's X/2 (X) and Y (Y). Top row ($B1-$C0): $3D57, $3D63, $3D6F; middle row ($C9-$D8): $3D94 (switch off), $3D8B, $3D78; bottom row ($E1 on): $3DAD, $3DB1, $3DB5, the three colour keys.

Decodes a fire on the three keys at the left of the panel (hand X/2 $13-$1B): top key (Y below $BF) scrolls the memory forward ($7A9F), middle key (Y $C8-$D6) back ($7B32), bottom key (Y $E0 on) is the phone ($7BC2).

Decodes a fire inside the display (hand X/2 $28-$79, Y below $DF): the slot from Y (row 0 or 3) and X/2 (columns at $40, $48-$5F, $64 on), 0-5 in Y. Fire on the slot already chosen ($8F) picks it up; on another, checks the slot holds a piece (memory slots $4EF5/$4EF6 for slots 0 and 3) or plays the low error tone ($3F41 with $2C/$C1), then selects it: hides the hand, shows the piece as sprites 4 and 5 at the slot's position ($720C/$7212) in its colour ($98,y), and sets $9F = 0 with the hand's limits $A0-$A3 for the display.

Top-middle button: click, flip the selected piece left to right ($7968), redraw the pieces.

Tells PAL from NTSC: waits for raster line 259 (low byte 3 after a value above $FC) and watches the raster register. On an NTSC machine (263 lines) it wraps to 0 before reaching $20 and nothing changes; on PAL (312 lines) it reaches $20, and $6E is written into the operands at $AB2B, $AB39 and $AB49, adjusting the game for the PAL frame. The game was therefore written for NTSC timing. Live: the three operands read $6E in play on the PAL machine.
